correctness.rationale: Every segment pair intersection and endpoint split is computed in Q(sqrt(5)) using exact rational arithmetic; exact halfedge traversal yields 171 planar vertices, 390 edges, 221 faces, 220 bounded cells, a twelve-value exact area spectrum and total normalized area one. The six chosen distinct face indices have exact shoelace sum 1/20 of the total. Exhaustive nondecreasing multiset search of up to five among all twelve positive classes visits 6186 prefixes with no target; positivity makes all pruning valid, proving impossibility of any smaller union. The standalone checker is embedded; only one finite decagon is claimed. A separate exact size-six class-multiset sweep yields only (4,8,11,11,11,11) and (7,8,10,11,11,11), whose choices count 8,778,000 by binomial coefficients.

originality.rationale: Huber A401643 determines the largest signed area denominator for a regular decagon (20) but expressly leaves positivity open generally and illustrates only a nonagon positive case. Its signed equality does not imply a six-cell unsigned witness or minimum. Inoue–Watanabe classify a four-region arrangement from two congruent diagonals; it does not contain the simultaneous 45-segment arrangement or the exact support-size cutoff. Targeted published-record and literature searches yielded no equivalent or dominating statement. The full Huber Zenodo report could not be inspected, leaving explicit, material priority uncertainty. The exact two-pattern equality classification is likewise not a consequence of the signed formula.
residual_risks: Full text of Huber Zenodo 23841077 was inaccessible, so a decagon-specific construction in it cannot be excluded; exact priority remains provisional.
Unindexed computations or small-polygon reference tables may have the same six-cell result.

value.rationale: The 2026 area-lattice problem distinguishes signed realizations from positive unions; this finding solves the first small even non-prime-power decagon case and determines an exact six-cell cutoff, supported by a complete 220-cell/12-value area census. It gives a natural finite exact support theorem rather than an arbitrary subset sum or a routine rewrite of the signed denominator formula; no all-n resolution is claimed. The equality patterns and count give a complete classification of minimal positive solutions.
